name: Osh International Airport
before:
Kyrgyzstan's second busiest airport, 9 km north of Osh, and the main gateway to the south of the country and the Fergana Valley. It carried 1,210,576 passengers in 2016.

What makes it useful is how close it is to places in other countries. Andijan is 43 km away, Namangan 103 km and Tashkent 322 km, against 300 km to Bishkek, so for anything in the Fergana Valley this beats flying to the Kyrgyz capital.

The airport operates 24 hours a day with a 3,212 metre runway, rebuilt in 2019, and 14 parking stands. It takes aircraft up to a 767 as well as the full range of Soviet era types still flying in the region.

A new two storey terminal began construction in February 2025, which will lift capacity to 900 passengers an hour.

Marshrutka routes 107 and 142 serve the airport. It opened in 1974 and its international sector followed in 1992.
after:
The airport lies 9 km north of Osh and is a key transport hub for southern Kyrgyzstan and the Fergana Valley.

In a straight line, Andijan is about 43 km away and Namangan 103 km, while Tashkent and Bishkek are each about 300 km away.

It has a single runway of 3,212 metres. The airport dates from 1974, and a new terminal, planned to handle 900 passengers an hour, has been under construction since 2025.

claims.note: Was 'the main gateway to the south of the country and the Fergana Valley': 'gateway to' is barred by house style and 'main' has no second source. The president called Osh airport 'a key transport hub in Fergana region' when construction of the new terminal began (24.kg, 14 Feb 2025), and presented the terminal as part of developing aviation in the south; Wikipedia says the airport serves the southern region and is one of the largest in the Fergana Valley.

claims.claim: Andijan about 43 km and Namangan 103 km, Tashkent and Bishkek each about 300 km, in a straight line
claims.inAfter: In a straight line, Andijan is about 43 km away and Namangan 103 km, while Tashkent and Bishkek are each about 300 km away.
claims.note: The figures are Wikipedia's. The coordinates give straight lines of 42.1 km (Andijan, GeoNames 'Andijon'), 103.8 km (Namangan), 309.2 km (Tashkent) and 292.3 km (Bishkek), ratios 0.99 to 1.04, so these are straight-line distances and the text now says so; the old wording could be read as road distances. The old framing around them is cut (below). Review (24 Sep): Wikipedia's 322 km (Tashkent) and 300 km (Bishkek) are 4 and 3 per cent above the straight lines the coordinates give (309.2 and 292.3 km), so the text now says 'each about 300 km' for both rather than giving 322 as a straight-line figure; Andijan and Namangan match to within a kilometre.

claims.claim: a new terminal for 900 passengers an hour, under construction since 2025
claims.inAfter: a new terminal, planned to handle 900 passengers an hour, has been under construction since 2025
claims.note: Was 'A new two storey terminal began construction in February 2025, which will lift capacity to 900 passengers an hour'. The start date is disputed: the president laid the first capsule on 14 February 2025 (Wikipedia's date), while the construction ministry says construction work began on 25 April 2025 (24.kg, 26 Feb 2026), so the text says 2025. The operator repeated the 900 passengers an hour in December 2025, when it expected to finish in summer 2026; in February 2026 the ministry reported the frame 95 per cent done but first-floor work paused for design changes, and no report of completion was found by 24 September 2026, so no opening date is given. 'Two storey' is dropped: that was the February 2025 design (25,443 square metres); the ministry now describes 26,000 square metres in six blocks, with the design being amended.

claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and resting on 2016 traffic. The operator's site (airport.kg) gives no traffic by airport: its indicators page covers only cargo and Manas, and its finance and older news pages answered 502. The president's own page on the terminal came back without its text. Softened to 'a key transport hub' (above).

claims.claim: the main gateway to the south and the Fergana Valley
claims.wasBefore: and the main gateway to the south of the country and the Fergana Valley
claims.why: Reworded to 'a key transport hub for southern Kyrgyzstan and the Fergana Valley': house style bars 'gateway to', and 'main' has no second source.

Ten years out of date, and no 2025 or 2024 figure for Osh was found (the operator's site as above). The president's February 2025 figure of 3.9 million rising to 5.8 million between 2021 and 2024 is not used: it does not say whether it counts Osh alone or all the country's airports.

claims.claim: what makes it useful is how close it is to places in other countries
claims.wasBefore: What makes it useful is how close it is to places in other countries.
claims.why: The distances are kept, but not the advice built on them. The FCDO (Kyrgyzstan, updated 14 Sep 2026) says crossing the borders can be complex and border crossings can close at short notice, so being near Uzbek cities is not a dependable advantage; the FCDO line is held back (below) rather than added.

claims.wasBefore: Andijan is 43 km away, Namangan 103 km and Tashkent 322 km, against 300 km to Bishkek
claims.why: Reworded to say they are straight-line distances (coordinates); the figures are kept.

claims.claim: for anything in the Fergana Valley this beats flying to the Kyrgyz capital
claims.wasBefore: so for anything in the Fergana Valley this beats flying to the Kyrgyz capital
claims.why: Advice rather than fact, and it assumes easy border crossings for the Uzbek side of the valley; see the FCDO line held back below.

claims.wasBefore: The airport operates 24 hours a day

Reworded as 'a single runway of 3,212 metres' (OurAirports, Wikipedia).
Wikipedia alone; no second source reached (see the operator's site above).

A new two storey terminal began construction in February 2025, which will lift capacity to 900 passengers an hour.
claims.why: Reworded (see the terminal claim above): the start date is disputed between February and April 2025, and the two-storey design is being amended.

claims.wasBefore: It opened in 1974 and its international sector followed in 1992.
claims.why: 1974 is kept as 'The airport dates from 1974' (the president, Wikipedia). The 1992 international sector rests on Wikipedia alone (the operator's history page has nothing on Osh).

claims.claim: FCDO: border crossings can be complex and close at short notice
claims.why: Held back: FCDO advice that replaces nothing. The FCDO does not advise against travel to any part of Kyrgyzstan, but its regional risks page (updated 14 Sep 2026) says crossing the borders can be complex, to take local advice, to use only recognised crossings and that crossings can close at short notice. Relevant to anyone using Osh for Andijan or Namangan; for Andy to add if he wants, attributed to the FCDO.

quote: Crossing the borders can be complex, take local advice if you’re planning on crossing.
Only use officially recognised border crossings.
Border crossings can close at short notice.

claims.claim: old terminal to become domestic only; summer 2026 target; work paused in February 2026
claims.why: Held back: new detail on one publisher. Airports of Kyrgyzstan said in December 2025 that once the new terminal opens the existing one will handle only domestic flights, with completion due in summer 2026 (24.kg); in February 2026 the construction ministry reported first-floor work suspended for design changes (24.kg). No later report was found, so whether the new terminal is open by now is not known.

claims.claim: runway extension and reconstruction planned for 2026 to 2027
claims.why: Held back: new, and not confirmed as started. In February 2025 the president's office said the runway extension's design would be ready in 2025, the work was planned for 2026 and the runways at Bishkek and Osh would be rebuilt by 2027 (24.kg; Wikipedia says the same). No source from 2026 says the work has begun; if it has, it may affect flights.
